Issued at 227 AM MDT Thu Aug 6 2026

As a member of Generation X, one of the music genres I listen to one 
shift is 80s music. And I heard a song tonight that remains me of my 
main dilemmas over the next few days. And this song is by one of the 
greatest artists of that era of music, Madonna, And it was her first 
Top 10 hit back in 1984, the song "Borderline". The juxtaposition 
the weather and the song is criteria for potential hazards, 
mainly of the fire weather and heat variety, which could be
borderline the next few days. We will handle each hazard 
individually in the discussion. So we will see if the atmosphere
can keep on pushing criteria over the borderline of hazard 
criteria.

HEAT...The overall reasoning of the forecast remains the same this 
morning, with ridging over the Desert Southwest gradually building 
northward into the Great Basin and toward Wyoming. This will raise 
heights through Saturday, resulting in a more stable atmosphere and 
basically no chance of convection through that period. It is also 
raising 700 millibar temperatures, bring some of the over 20 degrees 
celsius variety starting Friday and continuing into Sunday. This 
will lead to another period of hot temperatures across the area, 
with some record highs once again possible. It will be hot today, 
with widespread 90s in the lower elevations East of the Divide, The 
really warm temperatures kick in starting Friday. The National Blend 
of Model Ensembles give a greater than 2 out of 5 chance of over 100 
degree temperatures from Worland to Thermopolis as well as locations 
under 5000 feet in the Wind River Basin and similar elevations 
around Casper. The heat looks to peak on Saturday, with most 
locations under 5300 feet having a 1 out of 2 chance of high 
temperatures over 100. Like the heat last weekend, the most hottest 
conditions should be in central Wyoming, where the warmest 
temperatures aloft will be. It may be a bit cooler on Sunday, 
probably similar to Friday. And even into Monday and Tuesday, it 
will remain quite hot. A bit cooler than the weekend but still above 
normal for this time of year. The main reasons for things being a 
bit cooler than in July are the smoke over the area, which may 
filter the sun a bit, along with the longer nights and somewhat 
shorter days allowing more cooling and less time to heat up during 
the day.

And this leads to the concern for possible Heat Advisories. The time 
of concern would be Friday into Sunday. It is borderline because dew 
points and humidity will remain very low. In addition, with the dry 
air and longer nights, most locations should cool into the 50s at 
night, providing some relief. So, we will hold off for now. The day 
shift can take another look today.

FIRE...The reasoning here is the same as yesterday as well. There is 
nearly an 100 percent chance of critical humidity  through the 
weekend, with some locations having humidity as low as 5 percent. 
The borderline condition is the wind. Unlike the past two heat 
waves, we will be closer to the top of the ridge. And this will 
bring more wind. For today, given the very low humidity and very dry 
fuels, we hedged toward issuing Red Flag Warnings. The area with the 
warnings is the area that has at least a 1 out of 2 chance of wind 
gusts over 25 mph for three hours this afternoon and evening. And it 
encompasses most of the southeastern portion of the county warning 
area.

We will still have to take this day to day. With the ridge building 
northward, it could decrease wind somewhat Friday and Saturday, 
especially for areas East of the Divide, dropping wind gusts below 
the borderline of Red Flag Criteria. I did give thought to a multi 
day Red Flag across southern Wyoming, especially Sweetwater County 
where wind is expected to remain rather gusty. But with still some 
uncertainty, we held off for now. Again, the day crew can take a 
look and see if we need to extend some of the warnings. These 
borderline conditions continue into the weekend as well. These 
concerns may finally begin to ease early next week as humidity 
starts to rise a bit and wind decreases somewhat.

We may see a bit of a pattern shift next week. The ridge will weaken 
somewhat and retreat to the south and east, allowing some monsoonal 
moisture to begin to slide up the backside of the ridge. We can't 
rule out a stray shower even late Saturday, but coverage would be 
very sparse. The chance does increase somewhat on Sunday, mainly 
across the west.  In addition, much of the moisture looks to be of 
the mid level variety so any shower or storm would produce more wind 
than rain. This looks to be the pattern into the middle of next 
week, with some convection possible each day but with precipitable 
waters remaining fairly close to normal, not a lot of rain. Some 
guidance indicates somewhat deeper moisture moving in for next 
weekend, but this is still 10 days out so uncertainty, needless to
